newsitem.title: USA: Christmas boosts December retail sales modestly.
newsitem.headline: Christmas boosts December retail sales modestly.

text.p: Christmas shopping boosted sales at retail stores modestly during December, the Commerce Department said Tuesday, as business picked up at clothing and general merchandise stores.

Total retail sales increased last month by 0.6 percent to a seasonally adjusted $208.2 billion after a revised 0.2 percent decline in November. That was slightly stronger than the 0.5 percent sales gain forecast by Wall Street economists.

Previously, the Commerce Department said total November retail sales had fallen by 0.4 percent. But it revised that to show a smaller decline. It also revised October sales up to a stronger 0.7 percent gain from the 0.3 percent rise it previously reported.

"Retail sales showed more strength than people anticipated, and point toward firmer growth in the fourth quarter," said Anthony Chan, chief economist at Banc One Investment Advisors. "That is underscored by strong upward revisions of overall retail sales in the prior month."
Sales of both long-lasting durable goods, like new cars, as well as non-durables such as food and clothing, rebounded in December from a November slump.

Sales of all types of durable goods rose 0.5 percent to $84.95 billion in December after a 0.4 percent drop in November, while sales of non-durables gained 0.7 percent to $123.24 billion following a 0.2 percent fall in November.
Earlier reports from major chain stores indicated that holiday sales were not as brisk as many had expected.

Despite strong job growth and rising incomes, consumers have held spending in check. Economists said that might help curb inflation, since consumer spending on goods and services fuels two-thirds of national economic activity.

"It is still questionable whether momentum will continue well into 1997," added Chan. "This is called into question by weakness in this month's eating and drinking sales. When consumers are optimistic, they tend to eat out more. It's a leading indicator of future retail activity."

Sales at general merchandise stores rose in December by 0.5 percent to $26 billion, recovering a 0.5 percent decline during November. At apparel stores, sales of clothing increased 1.5 percent to $9.43 billion after falling 1.7 percent in November.
Sales of new cars were stronger in December, rising 0.7 percent to $50.9 billion following a 1 percent drop in November.

New cars account for about one-fifth of total retail sales, so swings in demand strongly affect the overall monthly figures. Excluding cars, retail sales still were 0.6 percent higher in December after being flat in November.
Sales of building materials dropped 1.6 percent last month to $11 billion after a 0.7 percent decrease in November.
Sales at food stores rose 0.3 percent last month to $35.8 billion following a 0.1 percent November fall.
Gasoline service station sales increased 0.8 percent to $13.3 billion after rising 0.2 percent in November.
